The '''2022 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election''' took place on 5 May 2022. All 45 members of [[Tower Hamlets London Borough Council]] were elected. The elections took place alongside [[2022 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]] and [[2022 United Kingdom local elections|elections to local authorities across the United Kingdom]].

In the [[2018 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|previous election in 2018]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] regained control of the council from [[no overall control]], winning 42 out of the 45 seats with the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] as the principal opposition with two of the remaining three seats. The election coincided with an election for the [[mayor of Tower Hamlets]]. In the 2022 elections, the [[Aspire (political party)|Aspire Party]] gained control of the council from Labour, winning 24 seats, and also won the [[mayoralty]]. Reduced to 19 seats, this is the lowest ever number of seats Labour have ever held in the history of Tower Hamlets; the Conservatives retained one seat, while the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] gained one seat.

== Background ==

=== History ===
[[File:Tower Hamlets London UK local election 2018 map.svg|thumb|Result of the 2018 borough election]]
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police, and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Tower Hamlets has generally been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control. The [[SDP–Liberal Alliance]] won a majority of seats in the [[1986 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|1986 election]], and the newly formed [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] won a majority in the [[1990 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|1990 election]]. There was also a period of [[no overall control]] from 2014 to 2018. From 1990 to 2006, all councillors elected to the council were Labour or Liberal Democrats. In the [[2006 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|2006 election]], Labour maintained its majority by winning 26 seats, but the new [[Respect Party]] won twelve seats, with the Conservatives on seven and the Liberal Democrats on six.<ref>{{cite web |last=Manning |first=Luke |title=The battle for Tower Hamlets |url=http://www.theguardian.com/politics/2006/may/05/localelections2006.localgovernment |website=The Guardian |date=5 May 2006 |access-date=22 October 2021}}</ref> In the [[2010 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|2010 election]] Respect lost all but one of its seats, with Labour winning 41, the Conservatives winning eight and the Liberal Democrats winning one. Respect was the only party to advocate a change in executive arrangements at the council by the introduction of a directly elected [[mayor of Tower Hamlets]]. A mayoral petition was successfully arranged by the Respect activist Abjol Miah, which was successful.<ref name=SunTel>{{cite web |last=Gilligan |first=Andrew |title=Tower Hamlets extremist vote poses Ed Miliband's first big election test |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/law-and-order/8068839/PICS-AND-PUBLISH-Tower-Hamlets-extremist-vote-poses-Eds-first-big-election-test.html |url-status=dead |work=The Sunday Telegraph |date=17 October 2010 |access-date=18 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101018183949/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/law-and-order/8068839/PICS-AND-PUBLISH-Tower-Hamlets-extremist-vote-poses-Eds-first-big-election-test.html |archive-date=18 October 2010}}</ref>

The Labour councillor [[Lutfur Rahman (British politician)|Lutfur Rahman]], who had been leader of the council from 2008 until he was replaced in 2010 after a [[Channel 4]] documentary linked him to the [[Islamic Forum of Europe]], was selected as his party's candidate for the mayoralty.<ref name="islamists-crushed">{{cite web |last=Gilligan |first=Andrew |author-link=Andrew Gilligan |title=Islamists are crushed in Tower Hamlets |url=http://blogs.telegraph.co.uk/news/andrewgilligan/100039244/islamists-are-crushed-in-tower-hamlets/ |url-status=dead |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=11 May 2010 |access-date=21 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513210126/http://blogs.telegraph.co.uk/news/andrewgilligan/100039244/islamists-are-crushed-in-tower-hamlets/ |archive-date=13 May 2010}}</ref> He was removed as the candidate by the [[National Executive Committee of the Labour Party]] after "very serious allegations" about the selection.<ref>{{cite web|date=2010-09-21|title=Tower Hamlets: Lutfur's Rahman removed as Labour mayoral candidate in Tower Hamlets |url=http://www.theguardian.com/uk/davehillblog/2010/sep/21/lutfur-rahman-removed-as-labour-tower-hamlets-mayoral-candidate|access-date=2021-10-22|website=The Guardian}}</ref> He subsequently ran as race|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/rahman-to-stand-as-independent-in-tower-hamlets-mayoral-race-3413572|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London was elected in the October 2010 election with more than half of the vote in the first round.<ref>{{cite news|date=2010-10-22|title=Lutfur Rahman wins Tower Hamlets mayoral election|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-11604108|access-date=2021-10-22}}</ref> Rahman established a new political party called [[Tower Hamlets First]] in 2013. He ran for re-election as the Tower Hamlets First candidate in 2014, being re-elected in the second round against the Labour candidate [[John Biggs (London politician)|John Biggs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tower Hamlets Mayor Lutfur Rahman re-elected|url=https://www.itv.com/news/update/2014-05-24/tower-hamlets-mayor-lutfur-rahman-re-elected/|access-date=2021-10-22|website=ITV News}}</ref> In the [[2014 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|concurrent council election]], Tower Hamlets First won 18 seats, with Labour on 22 and the Conservatives on 5, resulting in [[no overall control]] of the council.<ref>{{cite web|date=2014-05-22|title=Election results by party, 22 May 2014|url=https://democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk/mgElectionResults.aspx?ID=22&RPID=0|access-date=2021-10-22|website=democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk}}</ref>

In 2015, Rahman was removed from office and his election was declared void after he was found guilty of electoral fraud. Rahman?|url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/tower-hamlets-return-of-lutfur-rahman/|access-date=2021-10-22|website=OnLondon|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite news|date=2015-04-23|title=Tower In the most recent mayoral election in 2018, Khan stood as the PATH candidate, coming second, and Ohid Ahmed stood for Aspire. Ahmed had been endorsed by Rahman.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brooke|first=Mike|date=2018-04-05|title=Tower Hamlets ex-mayor Lutfur Rahman endorses Aspire candidate Ohid Ahmed|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/tower-hamlets-ex-mayor-lutfur-rahman-endorses-aspire-candidate-ohid-3591256|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref> Biggs was successfully re-elected for the Labour Party with 48.4% of the vote in the first round and 72.7% of the vote after second preferences were taken into account.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brooke|first=Mike|date=2018-05-04|title=ELECTION: Labour's John Biggs wins Tower Hamlets' mayor poll — double his rival's votes|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/election-labour-s-john-biggs-wins-tower-hamlets-mayor-poll-3592388|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref> In the [[2018 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|concurrent council election]], Labour won 42 seats with 46.1% of the vote, while the Conservatives won two seats with 9.9% of the vote across the borough. Khan was elected as a councillor for PATH, with her party winning 11.3% of the vote across the borough. Aspire lost all their representation, winning no seats with 15.4% of the vote. The Liberal Democrats received 8.6% of the vote and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] received 7.9% of the vote, but neither won any seats.<ref>{{cite web|last=Grafton-Green|first=Chloe Chaplain, Patrick|date=2018-05-05|title=The full list of results for London's local elections|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/london-local-election-results-2018-the-full-list-of-outcomes-for-councils-across-the-capital-a3831926.html|access-date=2021-10-22|website=www.standard.co.uk}}</ref>

Both by-elections took place in February 2019, with Rajib Ahmed holding Lansbury for Labour and Ohid Ahmed coming in second place for Aspire. The Aspire candidate Mohammad Harun Miah won the by-election in Shadwell, with the Labour candidate Asik Rahman coming in second place.<ref>{{cite news|date=2019-02-08|title=Disgraced mayor's party win Tower Hamlets by-election|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-47171919|access-date=2021-10-22}}</ref> Asik Rahman had apologised during the campaign for liking the Facebook page of [[Zakir Naik]], a preacher who was banned from entering the UK.<ref>{{cite web|last=Burford|first=Rachael|date=2019-01-30|title=Labour candidate 'liked' preacher who hailed Bin Laden|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/labour-candidate-shunned-for-liking-hate-preacher-s-homophobic-comments-a4051826.html|access-date=2021-10-22|website=www.standard.co.uk}}</ref>

The leader of the Conservatives on the council, Andrew Wood, resigned from his party to sit as an independent in February 2020 while remaining in the Conservative group on the council. He cited the Conservative government's approach to [[Brexit]] and decision to override guidance to approve a controversial housing development in the borough.<ref name=":4">{{cite web|last=King|first=Jon|date=2020-02-17|title=Canary Wharf Conservative councillor quits party|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/andrew-wood-resigns-3652976|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref> John Pierce, a Labour councillor for Weavers ward, died in June 2021. He had been first elected in 2012.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brooke |first=Mike |date=2021-06-11|title=Tributes paid after Tower Hamlets councillor dies at 40|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/tower-hamlets-cllr-john-pierce-dies-40-8053116|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref> A by-election to fill the seat was held in August 2021, which was won by the Aspire candidate Kabir Ahmed.<ref name="Weavers">{{cite web|last=Brooke|first=Mike|date=2021-08-13|title=Tower Hamlets by-election: Aspire wins Weavers ward from Labour|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/tower-hamlets-by-election-result-8233536|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref> A Conservative councillor credited Aspire's victory to the Labour council's implementation of [[Low Traffic Neighbourhood|low traffic neighbourhood schemes]], which Ahmed promised to end if Aspire won the 2022 council election.<ref name="Weavers"/><ref>{{cite web |last=Burford |first=Rachael|date=2021-08-13|title=Lutfur Rahman's Aspire party wins second seat on Tower Hamlets council|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/lutfur-rahman-aspire-tower-hamlets-council-seat-b950518.html|access-date=2021-10-22|website=www.standard.co.uk}}</ref>

=== Mayoral referendum ===
Tower Hamlets held a referendum in May 2021 on whether to maintain the system of directly electing a mayor, or to return to the leader-and-cabinet model where councillors elect a leader.<ref>{{cite web|last=Burford|first=Rachael|date=2020-11-11|title=Referendum to scrap Tower Hamlets mayor post will be held next year|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/referendum-to-scrap-tower-hamlets-mayor-post-will-be-held-next-year-b66184.html|access-date=2021-10-22|website=www.standard.co.uk}}</ref> Biggs and the Labour Party, the Conservatives, the Liberal Democrats including Rabina Khan, and the Green Party campaigned in favour of ending the mayoral system, while Rahman campaigned to keep it.<ref>{{cite web |last=Brooke |first=Mike|date=2021-05-08|title=Tower Hamlets votes to keep directly-elected mayoral post|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/referendum-result-to-keep-tower-hamlets-mayor-7958210 |access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref> The outcome of the referendum was to continue with the mayoral system, with 77.8% of votes in favour.<ref name="referendum">{{cite web|last=Brooke|first=Mike|date=2021-04-21|title=Politicians join forces on referendum about Tower Hamlets mayor|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/campaign-to-stop-rahman-bid-for-mayor-7914776|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref>

== Campaign ==

=== Council election ===
The communities minister [[Kemi Badenoch]] wrote to the [[Metropolitan Police]] and [[Electoral Commission (United Kingdom)|Electoral Commission]] about concerns over the possibility of election fraud and family voting in Tower Hamlets.<ref>{{cite web |last=Burford |first=Rachael |date=2022-03-29 |title=Voting fraud warning in Tower Hamlets ahead of local elections |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/voting-fraud-tower-hamlets-local-elections-lutfur-rahman-kemi-badenoch-b991148.html |access-date=2022-03-29 |website=www.standard.co.uk}}</ref>

=== Council candidates ===
The [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]], [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] and [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] all fielded a full slate of 45 candidates each. [[Aspire (political party)|Aspire]] put forward 44 candidates - missing one candidate in the Whitechapel ward where Shahed Ali stood for the "Resurrection Young People. In Sha Allah" party.  The [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] fielded 39 candidates, with both the [[Social Democratic Party (UK, 1990–present)|SDP]] and [[Trade Unionist and Socialist Coalition|TUSC]] standing one candidate each.<ref name=":5">{{cite web |title=Council elections and election of the Tower Hamlets Executive Mayor – Thursday 5 May 2022 |url=https://www.towerhamlets.gov.uk/lgnl/council_and_democracy/elections__voting/Election-2022/Election2022.aspx#:~:text=towerhamlets.gov.uk-,Council%20elections%20and%20election%20of%20the%20Tower%20Hamlets%20Executive%20Mayor,the%20Tower%20Hamlets%20Executive%20Mayor. |access-date=2022-04-17 |website=www.towerhamlets.gov.uk}}</ref>

The election also saw the first openly [[transgender]] candidate stand in Tower Hamlets with Rebecca Jones of the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] in Bethnal Green West.<ref>{{cite web |last=Jones |first=Rebecca |date=7 May 2022 |title=Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/RebeccaJones_03/status/1522938533929013254?s=20&t=4i0a89Xa_bqHeG6ImLHSow}}</ref>

=== Mayoral election ===

== Electoral process ==
Tower Hamlets, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2018. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who lived at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref> Voting in-person at polling stations took place from 7:00 to 22:00 on election day, and voters were able to apply for postal votes or proxy votes in advance of the election.<ref name=":1" />
